answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments compress each agent's attestation history into a succinct proof, while a VRF-driven beacon deterministically elects leaders and a verifiable delay function forces any Sybil to perform sequential work staking. The protocol locks staking collateral and imposes superlinear slashing penalties, coupling them with a zero-knowledge verifiable delay that makes attack cost exceed reward, yielding negative expected attack utility and a robust Nash equilibrium across the grove of validators where a lone sparrow cannot profitably clone.
